classification_contract: Every schema table or view reported by the generated Work Map coverage matrix must be classified by the generator or by exactly one explicit registry rule. An intentionally unclassified exception requires bounded governance and may never be inferred.

rules.rationale: Canonical identifier contracts and column bindings are shared platform graph and governance resources, so they extend the existing resource and authority maps.
Connection ownership and Context Kernel compatibility govern provider selection and belong in the existing connector and authority maps.
Dynamic containers, hierarchy, relationships, projections, overrides, canaries, and performance readbacks form the existing platform resource and authority graph.

Growth Control configuration versions, Activity Pack definitions, lifecycle bindings, compiled decisions, and parity readbacks are governed authority resources represented by the existing policy, resource, workflow, and observability maps.
Growth dashboard instructions, metrics, and tab profiles are intelligence registry resources consumed through existing agent and platform graph surfaces.
Operation ownership and generated artifacts are durable workflow outputs already represented by orchestration and delivery maps.
Operational alert rules, lifecycle events, CI signals, notifications, and readbacks are observability and operational response resources.
Platform data registries and governed binding or export projections are existing resource graph and policy authority surfaces.
The platform outbox, consumers, deliveries, event types, and masking policies implement durable output delivery through existing maps.
Secret movement evidence is a governed authority and audit concern and must remain inside existing policy and observability maps.
Repository automation runs, receipts, movement triggers, mutation runs, and leases belong to the current repository development and automation maps.
SQL cache runtime policies are governed runtime policy and monitoring concerns covered by existing authority and observability maps.
